transcript: Today, my boyfriend Paul and I saw I Need That on Broadway, a new play starring Danny DeVito as an old man named Sam living in New Jersey with way too much stuff. When his obsession with holding onto relics of the past make him vulnerable to possible eviction, his friend and his daughter help him try to clean up and move on. Honestly, this play surpassed my expectations because the premise didn't really sound that interesting to me. While the first third of it is mostly the characters arguing about the state of Sam's home with Sam stubbornly holding onto all of his possessions, it does end up being about more than just that. And the writing is heartfelt and funny, there's a really great scene where Sam is playing board game by himself. But, despite some great moments, I honestly didn't find this piece particularly memorable or necessary. With that, another playbill for my collection.
